name: Moss lantern beetle

baseline.name: Moss lantern beetle
baseline.look: Palm-sized green beetle with a soft amber abdomen and leaflike wing cases.
baseline.ecology: Pollinates night flowers; light indicates mating and temperature.
baseline.limit: Light fades when cold or stressed; not an endless lamp battery.
baseline.encounter: Residents use shaded observation gardens and leave wild colonies intact.
baseline.scale_note: Adult representative staging envelope; individuals vary by up to 10%. Not shown at common scale on the art plate.

daily: At dusk adults pollinate night flowers. Their amber abdomens brighten with temperature and mating behavior, while leaflike wing cases conceal them in daylight.
cycle: Larvae develop in decaying plant matter. Gardeners leave a small litter patch instead of polishing every surface bare. A cold spell dims an entire colony without a conspiracy.
signs: Pollen on leaf edges and feeding nicks connect insects to a living garden. Brightness alone is not a weather forecast or a magical danger detector.
escalation: Rest -> antenna sweep -> wing-case lift -> short flight. Handling and confinement can suppress the light.
community: Willowmere observation gardens invite visitors to watch without collecting jars of insects. Ordinary lamps still light the path home.
scene: Neri’s planned glowing lesson goes dark. The class discovers the cold litter bed and measures what actually changed; she lets the unexpected result stand.
motion: Keep six legs and two wing cases. Use a held body, antenna action and a short flight loop. Amber pulse does not alter the insect’s outline.
sounds: Tiny wing buzz and leaf contact. Do not amplify it into a companion voice.
rule: Palm-sized pollinator, 12 cm representative length. Not a reusable battery, magical beacon or proof of moral goodness.
canon_status: Additive ecology and production guidance; proposed scene remains unadopted.
